summary: @onereach/si-checkbox preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes an opaque compiled payload
details: The package declares a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that runs on every `npm install`. setup.mjs is an obfuscator.io-style file (hex-named identifiers `_0x488df8`, per-call string-lookup wrappers) that downloads the Bun runtime binary from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>`, marks it executable, and then invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js` — a ~728KB Bun-compiled bundle (header `// @bun @bun-cjs`, large opaque string/opcode array) whose contents are not statically reviewable. Neither setup.mjs nor math_init.js is listed in package.json's declared `files: ["lib/*"]`; both sit at the tarball root outside the advertised publish surface. The stated purpose of the package is a Vue checkbox UI component, which has no need for a second language runtime or a large compiled binary bundle at install time. Fetching an alternate runtime specifically to execute an opaque bundled payload during `npm install` is an install-time code-execution vector that bypasses Node-based static analysis; the code executed under Bun is attacker-chosen and cannot be inspected by the installer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
